text_blocks.snippet: High levels of uric acid, also known as hyperuricemia, can lead to several symptoms, most notably gout and kidney stones. Gout is characterized by sudden, severe joint pain, often in the big toe, along with swelling, redness, and warmth. Kidney stones can cause sharp pain in the back, side, or abdomen, as well as nausea, vomiting, and changes in urination.
snippet_highlighted_words: sudden, severe joint pain, often in the big toe, along with swelling, redness, and warmth

list.snippet: Sudden, severe joint pain: Typically in the big toe, but can affect other joints like ankles, knees, elbows, wrists, and fingers.
Swollen, red, and warm joints: The affected joint may be tender to the touch.
Difficulty moving the joint: Limited range of motion due to pain and inflammation.
Bumps and swelling on the joints: Uric acid crystals can form deposits, causing visible lumps.
Sharp, intense pain: In the lower back or side, sometimes radiating to the abdomen or groin.
Pain or burning during urination: Difficulty or pain when urinating.
Changes in urination: Increased frequency, urgency, or cloudy, foul-smelling urine.
Blood in the urine: May be visible or microscopic.
Nausea and vomiting: Can be triggered by the pain associated with kidney stones.
Fever and chills: If a urinary tract infection develops alongside the kidney stones.
Elevated uric acid levels may not always cause noticeable symptoms until a gout flare-up or kidney stone develops, according to Gout Education.
In some cases, chronic high uric acid levels can contribute to kidney damage and chronic kidney disease, says Verywell Health.
Long-term complications of gout can include joint damage and reduced mobility, according to Big Apollo Spectra Hospital.
